strengths: Strong and consistent experimental results: BD-rate improvements of -15.91%, -21.34%, -17.58% over VTM-21.0 across three benchmarks, with clear advantages over other Mamba-based LIC models
Excellent computational efficiency: Significantly more efficient than MambaIC (69.11M vs 157.09M parameters, 57% GPU memory reduction, 25% faster decoding) while achieving superior compression

weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Token clustering and prompt-based conditioning are existing techniques; main contribution is incremental combination for LIC with only moderate individual gains (CTA: 1.7-2.2%, GPP: 0.7-1.2% BD-rate)

Critical ablations missing: Number of clusters K (fixed at 64), K-means iterations per step (fixed at 5), EMA decay parameter λ, sequence reordering computational cost, cluster initialization sensitivity, and comparisons with random clustering

Experimental fairness issues: MambaIC comparison depends on authors' reconstruction quality; different entropy models vs. TCM prevent direct architectural comparison; iso-parameter comparisons not provided

strengths: Comprehensive and convincing empirical results: Strong BD-rate improvements (15-21%) over VTM-21.0 across three diverse benchmarks (Kodak, Tecnick, CLIC) at different resolutions

Thorough experimental evaluation: Includes proper metrics (BD-rate, BD-PSNR, MS-SSIM), detailed complexity analysis showing favorable trade-offs (57% memory reduction vs MambaIC), and ablation studies demonstrating component contributions

Technical soundness and clarity: The method is coherent, implementable, and well-described with useful visualizations (ERF in Figure 7, clustering results in Figure 8) providing intuitive understanding

Favorable complexity-performance balance: Achieves SOTA compression while maintaining linear Mamba complexity (69.11M parameters, 2.39T FLOPs, significantly better than MambaIC with 157.09M parameters and 5.56T FLOPs)
weaknesses: Limited novelty with primarily incremental contributions: K-means token clustering is a straightforward application of standard techniques; prompt dictionary is directly borrowed from Guo et al. (2024a); the approach combines existing techniques without fundamental innovation

Critical ablations missing: No ablation on cluster count K (fixed at 64), K-means iterations per step (fixed at 5), or comparison of clustering methods (only cosine similarity tested); these are fundamental hyperparameters

Incomplete understanding of computational costs: K-means overhead claimed as 5% but scaling with resolution unclear; training time not reported; inference cost breakdown missing; computational cost during training (quadratic for K-means) not fully accounted

Comprehensive evaluation with multiple metrics (PSNR, MS-SSIM, BD-rate), ablation studies clearly showing individual component contributions (CTA: 1.7-2.2%, GPP: 0.7-1.2%)

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly identifies two specific limitations of Mamba for image compression (content-agnostic raster scan and strict causality) with strong intuition for why they matter.
Strong experimental results: Achieves significant BD-rate improvements (15.91%-21.34% over VTM-21.0) and substantially outperforms recent Mamba-based LIC methods (MambaVC, MambaIC).

Comprehensive evaluation: Thorough ablations isolating component contributions, ERF visualizations showing content-adaptive receptive fields, cluster visualizations validating semantic grouping, and testing across multiple datasets.

Technical soundness and stability: Codebook-based K-means with EMA updates ensures stable training (demonstrated across random seeds), efficient inference without iterative updates, and proper permutation handling.
Good complexity-performance trade-off: Achieves 78% GPU memory reduction vs. MambaIC while improving performance; maintains comparable FLOPs and latency to prior methods.

Effective visualizations and analysis: Per-image ERF analysis demonstrates genuine content-adaptivity aligned with semantic structures; cluster visualization effectively shows fine-grained semantic grouping.
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core components are adaptations of existing ideas—codebook clustering from VQ-VAE, K-means clustering is standard, prompt-based conditioning well-known. Contribution is primarily in combination rather than fundamental innovation.

Concurrent similar work not fully distinguished: Zhang et al. (2024) also uses clustering for content-adaptive LIC. While methodological differences are argued, the core idea of clustering-based content adaptation is similar. The distinction between coarse and fine-grained clustering somewhat subjective.

Prompting mechanism lacks principled design: The modification O_i = (C + P)h_i + Dx_i appears ad-hoc; why is this the correct way to inject global priors? Alternative designs not explored. Why modulate C specifically rather than other matrices? Limited theoretical justification.

Questionable causality mitigation claims: GPP alone contributes only 0.5-1.4% (Table 2) versus CTP's 1.8-2.4%, suggesting the causality issue may not be the primary limitation. The prompt P derives from same tokens being processed, not truly external global information.

Insufficient justification for design choices: Why T=5 K-means iterations? Why K=64 when typically only 23-26 clusters active (Table 5)? EMA decay λ value not specified in main paper. First-batch centroid initialization could be unstable. Initialization of prompt dictionary U not discussed.
Code not yet released: Paper states code 'will be released later,' limiting verification and reproducibility. Some implementation details remain unclear despite lengthy appendix.
Limited cross-dataset evaluation: Trained only on Flickr2W; generalization to other datasets/domains not thoroughly tested. Only three test datasets used.

Entropy model confounds evaluation: While not claimed SOTA, the enhanced SCCTX entropy model contributes to performance. Table 8 shows some performance metrics drop when using FTIC's entropy model, though still competitive.
